verdicts.why: Names a manner of speaking (forthright, candid) without approving or scorning it; the sentences even use the older 'at once' sense, and neither judges.
A footrace of a fixed length is a plain referent with no attitude in the word.
A unit of length; pure measurement, no judgement.
A nautical unit of length; pure measurement, no judgement.
An ancient unit of length; pure measurement, no judgement.
A Swedish unit of length; pure measurement, no judgement.
Refraining from a food or drink is stated flatly; the verb takes no side on the abstainer or the food.
A legal term for declaring something invalid; technical and neutral.
A party favour is a plain object name with no attitude toward giver, guest, or gift.
Making someone do something is stated as fact; unlike 'boss around' or 'dictate', the verb neither approves nor resents the demand.
A risk is an unpleasant referent, but 'chance' names it plainly without the speaker's attitude, unlike 'gamble' or 'folly'.
A measure of likelihood; purely descriptive.
A place where work is done (the works) is a plain location name.
An author's or artist's output is named without praise or dismissal.
Study as an activity is described, not judged; 'grind' or 'cramming' would carry the attitude, 'work' does not.
A physics quantity; technical and attitude-free.
Playing a role is a plain description of what a performer does.
Pretending is the meaning of the sense, not an attitude on top of it; 'act surprised' reports the pretence as neutrally as 'feign' does, where 'put on' or 'pose' would sneer.
Having an effect (a drug acts quickly) is flat description.
Discharging one's duties is named without approval or contempt.
Saying a play acts well is a stage-craft description, not a loaded word.
Establishing communication with someone is stated neutrally.
Forming a relationship is named plainly; the sentences' snobbery about 'connecting with such a family' lives in the context, not in the verb.
Joining for communication is a plain technical description.
Joining by communication equipment is a plain technical description.
